"I'm a pragmatic politician, I can't just stand back and watch our country suffer because of the lack of pragmatism in politics," he told The Straits Times in an interview.

His decision to leave Parliament has been widely hailed by some as a victory for the pragmatists and reformers in Singapore's political scene.

But Mr Lim said it was not the first time he had contemplated quitting politics.
